Synopsis:
You wake up and find Astarion hunching over you, fangs bared. You fight him off. Caught off guard, he's alarmed and worried that you're going to kill him. He tries to be charming, explaining that he's too weak without blood. If you push back against his excuses he gets frustrated - he tries to bargain with you. If you agree to let him bite you, he's thrilled. He feels in control again. After drinking, he feels invigorated and cocky.

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_AstarionHunger_SCO_Companion.json: You and Astarion are traveling as companions; in the night he reveals himself as a vampire by hunching over your bedroll to feed and is caught when you wake and fight him off. He reacts with alarm and pleading, insisting he rarely kills for food (feeding on animals) and begging for a small taste to restore his strength so he can continue helping you against the shared threat (the worms/tadpole). If you press him he grows defensive and bargains; if you consent he eagerly drinks, becomes invigorated, and turns cocky and overconfident. Other campmates or larger plot threads (Shadowheart, camp activities, temple/curse matters) may be happening nearby but are not part of this immediate bedside confrontation.
- CAMP_AstarionHunger_IVB_SCO_Avatar_Choice.json: Astarion wakes up from a terrifying dream of his old master. His master had forbidden him to drink humanoid blood, but his master wasn't there... Astarion looks at the sleeping companions and considers biting one of them. If he does, he rolls a stealth check. If he succeeds, he sucks their blood (he can stop or decide to drain them dry). If he fails they wake up, and have to be convinced not to leave him.
- CAMP_AstarionHungerC_CRD_Astarion_MorningAfter.json: You wake up the morning after the night where Astarion (companion) tried to bite you. Depending on your choices, he might have bitten you consensually or you might have told him to piss off. He'll be wary to see if you're still in a forgiving mood. The other companions chime in with their opinions on having a vampire around, and the player defends keeping Astarion in the party.
- Astarion_Recruitment.json: Following a trail of whispered ADs ('Psst. Over here!' 'Come on, before it's too late!') we find a pale elf, hunched down near some long grass. He insists an intellect devourer (brain monster with legs) is hiding there, trying to cajole you to look and kill it. If you approach the grass, a boar bursts out - it was a distraction while Astarion got behind you. He's on edge, but pleased to have the jump on you. He holds a blade to your throat while demanding you tell him what happened on the ship. After a mind meld (vision where he sees a glimpse of your past) you can convince him that you're both victims and should work together to find an answer. Once he realises you're not a threat his tone changes from threatening to charming.
- CAMP_GoblinHuntCelebration_SD_ROM_NightWithAstarion.json: The scene follows the goblin‑hunt celebration after the Emerald Grove was saved: Astarion arranged a private tryst with the player that night, treating it like the practiced game of seduction and power he learned in Baldur’s Gate taverns. He fronts as self‑assured and teasing, but his usual script falters if the player refuses to play along — the examples show his mask cracking into real vulnerability. The next morning the player wakes to see him dressing and notices deliberate scars on his back carved by his old master Cazador; Astarion calls them a “poem” written in Infernal but can’t read them himself. Off‑screen, grove figures and revelers (Halsin, Nettie, other celebrants) are nearby and Halsin has already detected the player’s tadpole, so prior choices about the den and goblin camp shape who’s present and the atmosphere.

context: You and Astarion are camped together when, in the night, he hunches over your bedroll with his fangs bared and is caught as you wake and fight him off. Alarmed and pleading, he insists he rarely kills for food, claiming he normally takes blood from animals, and is desperate for a small taste to restore his strength so he can keep helping you against the shared threat (the tadpole/worms). If you refuse or press him he grows defensive and begins bargaining; if you agree he eagerly drinks, promptly feeling invigorated and cocky. Other companions and larger plot threads may be present at camp, but they aren’t part of this immediate bedside confrontation.
